page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processors using the x86_64 architecture, clocked at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance configuration supplies 128 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio that equates to 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for all file system and persistent data needs. In addition, it features no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, though it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured networking solutions for external access.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the high compute density of 128 cores delivers substantial processing scale on a single node without allocating surplus memory overhead. The primary design tradeoff is the complete reliance on network-attached storage and the absence of local NVMe scratch space, which shifts I/O profiles entirely to network and storage fabric performance.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.32xlarge is suited for horizontally or vertically scaled CPU-bound workloads that do not demand extensive RAM-per-core allocations. Typical production deployments include large-scale batch processing, continuous integration and build pipelines, CPU-driven computational modeling, video encoding, and high-throughput web frontends.
